sentences: `image_sample*_o`: the first address dword packs signed 6-bit offsets (x [5:0], y [13:8], z [21:16]), which become the SPIR-V `Offset` operand.
A non-constant `Offset` outside gather needs **`VK_KHR_maintenance8`**, and is validated with `spirv-val --allow-offset-texture-operand`.
The operand is always a run-time value: the translator extracts the fields from the register, also when the shader loaded the dword from an immediate, so every `_o` sample needs the extension.
`image_gather4_lz_o` / `_l_o` read x and y the same way; a gather `Offset` needs `shaderImageGatherExtended`, not maintenance8.

**GPU-tested** with `runtime/test/shaders/ps_texoff.asm` on `vk_texture_test` (in `check.py` and `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py`; SKIP on a device without the extension), on an AMD Radeon RX 6800, Windows driver 26.11.2, maintenance8 enabled: an 8×8 texture whose texels are all different, a point sampler that clamps to the edge, 2D targets, mip 0.

`image_sample_lz_o` with an offset computed per pixel (all 64 pairs of x, y in −4..3, none clamped), `image_sample_l_o` with (−3, +2) and `image_sample_lz_o` with (+16, −32) from immediates, and `image_gather4_lz_o` of red and of green with the per-pixel offset gave, on all 4096 pixels, the texels worked out by hand from this rule (derivation in the `.asm` header).

Run with a sabotaged translator, the test fails when the sample offset is dropped, has x and y swapped, takes y from bit 6, or uses 4-bit or 5-bit fields, and when the gather offset is dropped, has x and y swapped or takes y from bit 6; 4-bit and 5-bit gather fields pass, because the gather offsets stay in −4..3.
What it shows is that the translated SPIR-V implements this rule on Vulkan; it does not measure the field layout on the hardware.

**It cannot see the sign extension on this driver**: with the fields read unsigned the same texels come back: `Offset` 60..63 sampled as −4..−1 and +32 as −32 (the device reports texel offset limits −64..63, gather −32..31).

The sign extension and the gather field width are therefore pinned by the structural test `tests/test_texel_offsets.py` (signed, bit 8k, 6 bits, for `_lz_o`, `_l_o`, `_o`, 3D and gather) and are not GPU-tested through Vulkan.

**The x field is measured on hardware:** `image_sample_lz_o` run as a raw compute kernel on the same RX 6800 (gfx1030, wave32 and wave64), on a 64×1 `R32_FLOAT` image whose texel i holds i, with a point sampler that clamps to the last texel: from texel 40, offset dword `0x20` reads texel 8 and `0x3c` reads texel 36 (unsigned would clamp both to 63); from texel 10, `0x1f` reads 41 and `0x20` clamps to 0; `0x40`, `0x80` and `0xc0` read the centre texel (bits 6–7 are ignored); and a non-zero y field, z field or top byte leaves x alone.
All 36 rows fit x = sign-extended bits [5:0].

**The y and z fields are measured too** (SHADER-337): `tools/texoff_probe.py --oracle hw` on the integrated GPU of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (gfx1036, RDNA2, Windows driver 32.0.21045.16010), wave32 and wave64, samples a linear `R32_SFLOAT` texture whose texel holds its index (2D 64×64 for y, 3D 64×1×64 for z) with `image_sample_lz_o` and a point sampler that clamps to the last texel.

From row 40, y = `0x20` reads row 8 and `0x3c` row 36, `0x21` row 9 (unsigned would clamp all three to 63); from row 10, `0x1f` reads 41 and `0x20` clamps to 0 (unsigned: 42); `0xc0` (bits 14–15 set, field 0) reads row 40 and `0x7f` row 39, so those bits are ignored; x −2 with y −4 in one dword reads both.
The z field at bits [21:16] gives the same 7 results on the 3D image.

All 15 rows fit each field = sign-extended 6 bits, the bits above it ignored, which is the translator's rule; `tests/test_texoff_probe.py` checks that every row with a negative field tells the signed reading from the unsigned one.
The (+16, −32) sample is outside Vulkan's guaranteed −8..7 and is judged only where the device limits cover it.

**`image_sample_o`, `image_sample_b_o` and `image_gather4_l_o` are GPU-tested** with `runtime/test/shaders/ps_texoff_forms.asm` (the same texture, sampler and per-pixel offset as `ps_texoff`, all 64 offset pairs in −4..3; in `check.py` and `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py`): 4096/4096 pixels exact on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 621.24) and on the integrated GPU of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (gfx1036, driver 32.0.21045.16010), both with maintenance8 enabled.

Not GPU-tested: `_c_lz_o`, the z field (3D), 1D, 2D-array and cube targets (offset next to an array layer), wrap or mirror addressing, linear filtering, mips other than 0, other vendors' drivers, and a device without maintenance8 (the test skips there; the translator has no fallback for it).

**Without maintenance8 (`--texel-offset-fallback`, NVIDIA Pascal for one):** an `image_sample*_o` gets no `Offset`; the offset is folded into the coordinate instead, as coordinate + offset ÷ the size of the sampled level.
The level is 0 for `_lz` / `_c_lz`, the given LOD for `_l`, and `OpImageQueryLod`'s for implicit samples (plus the bias for `_b`), floored and clamped to the image's levels.
A texel offset applies before wrapping and clamping, and an integer offset commutes with both, so the shift is exact for every address mode at that level.
The one case that differs is a trilinear blend of two levels, where the coarser level moves by offset ÷ 2 of its texels.

Implicit samples become `Grad` samples with the derivatives of the unshifted coordinate (× 2^bias for `_b`), so the LOD and anisotropy are those of the original sample even when the offset varies per pixel.
Gathers keep their `Offset` (`shaderImageGatherExtended`).
Only 4 of the 12,101 PS need it, all through `image_sample_o`.

**GPU-tested** on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (no maintenance8; driver 560.94, Windows 10) with `LEONIDA_TEXOFF_FALLBACK=1`: `ps_texoff` and `ps_texoff_implicit` (the per-pixel sample as `image_sample_o`) are 4096/4096 pixels exact, with the +16/−32 sample judged too, since a coordinate shift has no device offset limit.
Checked in `tests/test_texel_offsets.py`, including `spirv-val` without `--allow-offset-texture-operand`.
